summary: Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. Sze completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia (~2006–2012) under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen and committee member Daniel L. Overmyer.
Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Kameyama has served as a Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University.

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1946–1953). He served as President of Ryukoku University (1970–1995) and as Chairman of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai.

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Matsumoto Fukashi High School, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1900–1902), Waseda University (~1902–1905), and the University of Paris (~1916–1920). He held a post at Waseda University (~1906–1940) and taught Kangei Okamoto.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1996–2002) and became a Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami and Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, later mentored by Heinz Bechert. Fukita held posts at Bukkyo and Kyoto universities.
Takanobu Takahashi (1951–2017) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held a post at Shitennoji University and served as an Associate Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1993–2017).

Takanori Kimura (born 1947) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Komazawa University. Kimura served as a Research Assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1977), a lecturer (講師) at Yamaguchi University, and chief priest (住職) at Kaichoji.

Takao Hayashi (born 1949) specializes in Indology and the history of archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1968–1977) and Brown University (~1979–1985) under David Pingree, later serving as Professor of History of Science at Doshisha University (~1989–2020).

Takao Kagawa (born 1926) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a Professor at Bukkyo University (~1969–1997) and taught Satoshi Hiraoka.

Takao Maruyama (born 1929) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held posts as assistant professor at Rissho University, emeritus professor at Shinshu University (~1965–1994), and professor at Mejiro University (~1994–2000).

Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) was a scholar of Central Asian history. After studying at Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, the University of Tokyo, and Osaka University, he held posts at Kanazawa University, Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, and Osaka University (Professor, ~1985–2013).

Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1951–1960). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1964–2003) and served as President of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (~1993–1997).

Takashi Hidaka is a Buddhist studies scholar. Hidaka worked as an open-call researcher (公募研究員) at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and held a post as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Otani University.

Takashi Iwata (born 1944) studied at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa and at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler and Lambert Schmithausen. A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, he was a Professor at Waseda (~1989–2015) and taught Florin Deleanu.
Takashi Maeda (born 1943) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1968–1974) and served as a lecturer (講師) at Taisho University.
Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Rissho University (~1950–1957) and later served there as an emeritus professor (~2002–2020).

Takashi Ogawa (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1980–1989) and Peking University (~1986–1988), and later served as an assistant professor (助教授) at Komazawa University (1999–2006).

Takashi Yamada (born 1954) is a scholar in sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University (~1974–1983). He served as an assistant professor (助教授) at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (~1994–2003).
Takatoshi Nakamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. Nakamura held an assistant (助手) post at Taisho University.
